newsitem.title: CHINA: HK, China bourses seen aided by cross-listings.
newsitem.headline: HK, China bourses seen aided by cross-listings.

text.p: The Hong Kong Stock Exchange and China's two bourses could benefit from more cross-listings of mainland Chinese shares, the head of the Hong Kong exchange was quoted on Saturday as saying.
As an international market, Hong Kong's stock exchange was unlikely to harm the interests of China's two young bourses, Edgar Cheng told the Shanghai Securities newspaper in an interview.

China's foreign currency B shares could be listed on the Hong Kong exchange, and H shares -- shares of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong -- could be listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges, he was quoted as saying.
These were some of the benefits to follow Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, he said.
The Hong Kong bourse would be able to help develop the mainland's capital markets and boost China's ability to compete with other Asian and international financial centres.

China's capital markets needed more capitalisation and advanced financial products and technology, Cheng said. Hong Kong was a ready-made source of international experience that China's markets could draw on.

"This systematic merging process should best benefit both Hong Kong and the mainland. It can't help but strengthen the development of China's capital markets, and will help Hong Kong become more competitive internationally," Cheng said.
The Hong Kong exchange said last week it saw itself as China's international bourse, with the bourses in Shenzhen and Shanghai playing a domestic role after July 1.

Mainland companies have recently offered shares in Hong Kong with phenomenal success. Last month, Beijing Enterprises was nearly 1,300 times oversubscribed and this week's offer by First Tractor was nearly 300 times oversubscribed.
